info.name: Armada API
info.description:
Complete API collection for the Armada multi-agent orchestration system.

Version: 0.9.0

## Setup
1. Set the `baseUrl` variable to your Admiral server (default: `http://localhost:7890`)
2. For bearer token auth, set `bearerToken` (default: `default`)
3. For session token auth, use the Authenticate request and set `sessionToken` from the response
4. Legacy: If API key authentication is enabled, set the `apiKey` variable (deprecated)
5. Use the Status > Health Check request to verify connectivity
6. For proxy requests, set `proxyBaseUrl`, run Proxy > Session > Login Challenge and Login, then Select Instance; relayed requests send `proxySessionToken`

## Role model
- IsAdmin=true: global system-wide admin
- IsAdmin=false and IsTenantAdmin=true: tenant-scoped admin
- IsAdmin=false and IsTenantAdmin=false: regular user with self-service on own account and credentials

## Notes
- Tenant, user, and credential protection is server-controlled through IsProtected
- Immutable fields such as IDs, ownership columns, and creation timestamps are preserved server-side on update
- Includes Objectives, Delivery workflow profiles, structured checks, environments, deployments, incidents, runbooks, releases, cross-entity history, Workspace, Planning Sessions, Request History, Mux runtime helpers, and OpenAPI discovery examples.

request.description: Deletes a subscription account, its persona routes and its server-derived login folder. Refused with account_has_captains while captains are assigned. Requires a global administrator.
Collects one account's usage now and reruns its login check. Honours a provider retry-after (usage_refresh_rate_limited). Requires a global administrator.
Creates the account's server-derived login folder (mode 0700). Idempotent. Requires a global administrator.
Starts the runtime's device or browser login in the account folder and returns only the verification URL and user code. Requires a global administrator.
Relays a pasted sign-in code to a pending paste-code login. The code is never returned or logged. Requires a global administrator.
Stores an OpenCode or Cursor API key in the account's credential file (mode 0600). The key is never returned or logged. Requires a global administrator.
Returns the pending login state and the server's login check for the account. Requires a global administrator.
Stops a pending login process. Requires a global administrator.

Returns the effective and stored global mode (effective Off with typed_decisions_no_key when no key resolves), whether a key is present and its source, and every decision's mode, threshold and description. Requires a global administrator.
Updates the global mode and per-decision modes and thresholds through the settings save path. Requires a global administrator.
Writes the provider key to the key file under the data directory (mode 0600). Returns 204 and never echoes the key. The environment variable, when set, still wins. Requires a global administrator.
Removes the key file and reports when the environment variable still supplies a key. Requires a global administrator.

item.name: Tenants
item.description: Tenant management endpoints. Global admin only for list/create/update/delete. Authenticated non-admin users may read only their own tenant by ID.

request.description: List all tenants (paginated). Global admin only.
Create a new tenant. Global admin only. The server seeds a protected admin@armada user and default credential for the new tenant. The seeded user is tenant admin only.
Get a tenant by ID. Global admin: any tenant. Tenant admin or regular user: own tenant only.
Update a tenant. Global admin only. Immutable fields such as Id, CreatedUtc, LastUpdateUtc, and IsProtected are server-controlled.
Delete a tenant. Global admin only. Returns 403 for protected tenants. Deleting an unprotected tenant cascades to all subordinate tenant resources, including protected child auth records.

item.name: Users
item.description: User management endpoints. Global admins can manage all users. Tenant admins can manage users within their tenant. Regular users can read and update only themselves.

request.description: List users (paginated). Global admins can list all users. Tenant admins can list users in their own tenant. Passwords are redacted.

Create a new user. Global admins can create users anywhere. Tenant admins can create users only in their tenant and cannot grant global admin. Password is plaintext in the request body and is hashed server-side. PasswordSha256 remains accepted for backward compatibility. IsProtected is server-controlled.
Get a user by ID. Global admin: any user. Tenant admin: users in own tenant. Regular user: own user only. Password is redacted.

Update a user. Global admins can update any user. Tenant admins can update users in their tenant. Regular users can update only themselves. If Password is supplied, the server hashes and stores the new password; if omitted, the existing password is preserved. Immutable fields such as Id, TenantId, CreatedUtc, LastUpdateUtc, and IsProtected are server-controlled.
Delete a user. Global admins can delete any unprotected user. Tenant admins can delete unprotected users in their tenant. Regular users cannot delete users directly. Returns 403 for protected users.

item.name: Credentials
item.description: Credential (bearer token) management endpoints. Admins can manage all; non-admins can manage their own.

request.description: List credentials (paginated). Global admin: all. Tenant admin: credentials in own tenant. Regular user: own credentials only.
Create a new credential with auto-generated bearer token. Global admin: any tenant/user. Tenant admin: users in own tenant. Regular user: self only. IsProtected is server-controlled.
Get a credential by ID. Global admin: any. Tenant admin: credentials in own tenant. Regular user: own only.

Update a credential. Global admins can update any credential. Tenant admins can update credentials in their tenant. Regular users can update only their own credentials. Immutable fields such as Id, TenantId, UserId, CreatedUtc, LastUpdateUtc, and IsProtected are server-controlled.
Delete a credential. Global admin: any. Tenant admin: credentials in own tenant. Regular user: own only. Returns 403 for protected credentials.

request.description: Updates editable server settings. When RemoteControl is supplied it replaces the full remoteControl object.
Initiates a graceful shutdown of the Admiral server. The server will stop after a brief delay.
Creates and streams a ZIP backup of the database and settings. Requires a global administrator.
Runs 7 system health checks and returns results as a JSON array.
Returns a consolidated, most-urgent-first list of items awaiting operator attention (reviews, failed landings, failed missions, stalled captains). Requires a global administrator.

Returns a tenant-scoped, evidence-based production baseline. It reports verified landed slices, dispatch delay, armed-to-start and execution timing, first-pass acceptance, rescue cost, closeout delay, post-land regressions, repeated research, eligible idle lane time, and explicit warnings for incomplete or unavailable evidence. Host-slot queue time stays unavailable until its start timestamp is durable.

Accepts a ZIP backup file in the request body and restores the database and settings. Server restart recommended after restore. Requires a global administrator. Destructive: replaces the database and settings from the uploaded ZIP backup. Send the backup file as the raw binary body.
Deletes database, logs, docks, and repos directories. Preserves settings file. Requires a global administrator. Destructive: deletes the database and the log, dock, and repository directories.

Re-reads settings.json and applies the runtime-tunable values in place, without a restart. Ports, paths, database, API key, agent definitions and remote-control settings are not reloaded and still require a restart. Requires a global administrator.
Preview preference-first usage admission. Requires a global administrator.

item.name: Build or Refine the Vessel Model Context

request.description: Launches the chosen captain in a worktree of the vessel repository to analyze it and write a Model Context document. Refines the existing context when one is present. Runs synchronously and can take several minutes. Requires a tenant administrator.
Updates only the ProjectContext and StyleGuide fields of a vessel. Requires a tenant administrator.
Returns commits ahead/behind the remote default branch for the vessel's working directory.
Predicts how Armada would land a branch for this vessel, including branch policy, check requirements, and likely blockers.
Returns readiness warnings and blocking issues for a vessel, optionally scoped to a requested workflow check.

Pushes one landing-repository branch to the vessel's configured origin without force. Requires a tenant administrator. Refusals name a reason code and change no refs. Outward action: the branch reaches the remote.

Merges one landing-repository branch into another by fast-forward or explicit merge commit. Strategy is FastForward or MergeCommit. Never pushes and never rewrites the target. Requires a tenant administrator.

item.name: Missions

request.description: Returns all missions with pagination. Supports filtering by status, vesselId, captainId, and voyageId.
Paginated enumeration of missions with full filtering support via JSON body.
Creates and dispatches a new mission. If a VesselId is provided, the Admiral will assign a captain and set up a worktree. Auto-saves the ID to the missionId collection variable.

request.description: Returns a single mission by ID.
Read GitHub pull-request review, comment, and required-check evidence for one mission.
Updates mission fields (title, description, priority). Does not change status -- use the status transition endpoint for that.

Transitions a mission to a new status.

Valid transitions:
- Pending -> Assigned, Cancelled
- Assigned -> InProgress, Cancelled
- InProgress -> Testing, Review, Complete, Failed, Cancelled
- Testing -> Review, InProgress, Complete, Failed
- Review -> Complete, InProgress, Failed
- Complete, Failed, Cancelled are terminal states
Transition from Assigned to InProgress.
Transition from InProgress to Complete.
Cancels a mission by setting its status to Cancelled.
Restarts a failed or cancelled mission by resetting it to Pending. Optionally update title and description before restarting. Body is optional.
Returns the git diff of changes made by a captain in the mission's worktree. Checks for a saved diff first, then falls back to a live worktree diff.
Returns the session log for a mission. Supports pagination via ?lines=N and ?offset=N query parameters.
Batch delete multiple missions by ID. Returns a summary of deleted and skipped entries.
Returns aggregated mission counts by time bucket for dashboard history charts.
Returns lightweight mission summaries without large description, diff, or agent-output payloads.
Paginated enumeration of lightweight mission summaries with optional filtering and sorting. Requires a tenant administrator.

Returns the vessel's current auto-land predicate, the latest recorded auto-land decision for the mission and the latest merge entry with its audit fields, in the caller's scope. Reading it evaluates no predicate and reads no diff.
Returns the current definition-of-done configuration for the mission and its latest recorded gate evaluation. Reading it runs no gate and does not change landing readiness.
Returns the runtime-specific instruction file generated for a mission, such as CLAUDE.md, CODEX.md, CURSOR.md, AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md, or MUX.md.
Predicts how Armada would land this mission, including branch policy, check requirements, and likely blockers.
Returns one redacted page plus the full safe artifact UTF-8 SHA-256 digest and explicit completeness state.
Permanently deletes a mission from the database. This cannot be undone. Destructive: permanently deletes the mission record.

Returns recorded recovery counters and budgets, rescue missions, linked incidents with runbook executions, and recent recovery events for the mission in the caller's scope. Reading it dispatches nothing and does not infer a landing from mission status.
Rebases the mission branch onto the current target and re-attempts landing. Only available for WorkProduced or LandingFailed missions. Requires a tenant administrator.
Approves a mission waiting at a review gate. Non-terminal stages continue to the next pipeline stage, and terminal stages continue to landing. Requires a tenant administrator.
Denies a mission waiting at a review gate. The mission either returns to Pending for rework or fails the pipeline, depending on its review policy. Requires a tenant administrator.
